extracted.intended_audience: graduate and advanced undergraduate students learning algebraic geometry (Math 216)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, constructions, and exercises for building and recognizing morphisms of schemes (and related foundational notions such as associated primes, primary ideals, Spec/Proj, and rational maps). Aimed at checking when a map is a morphism, how it is determined by ring maps or global sections, and how to glue/construct such maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated points are generic points of irreducible components
rubrics_metrics.description: For A Noetherian and M a finitely generated A-module: every associated point is the generic point of an irreducible component of Supp m for some m ∈ M; in particular p = Ann(m) for some m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part (a) of Exercise 5.5.P; use existence of m with Ann m = p to relate associated primes to irreducible components of supports. Useful also for Exercise 5.5.O.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of an element equals closure of associated points where its germ is nonzero
rubrics_metrics.description: If m ∈ M, the support of m is the closure of those associated points at which m has nonzero germ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is part (b) of Exercise 5.5.P. Hint: if p is in the closure of such an associated point show m has nonzero germ at p; if p is not in the closure, localize at p and use Theorem 5.5.10(b) (and 5.5.10(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated point for integral domains/schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: For an integral domain the unique associated prime is (0); for an integral scheme the unique associated point is its generic point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt (A) as the definition and establish (B) and (C) as in Exercise 5.5.Q. Consequence: rational functions on an integral scheme X are precisely elements of the function field K(X) (Definition 5.2.H).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal-prime elements are zero-divisors (without Noetherian hypothesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p is a minimal prime of A and s ∈ p, then s is a zero-divisor (argument via localization: pAp is the unique prime of Ap, so s/1 is nilpotent and hence s becomes a zero-divisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This remark in 5.5.12 shows the fact holds without Noetherian hypotheses and is used in Exercise 11.1.G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of primary ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal I in a ring A is primary if xy ∈ I implies either x ∈ I or y^n ∈ I for some n>0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associated primes of an ideal are precisely the radicals of ideals occurring in any primary decomposition. Historical note: Lasker introduced primary decomposition; Noether axiomatized it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of ringed spaces (basic data)
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of ringed spaces π: X → Y consists of a continuous map of topological spaces π together with a map of sheaves O_Y → π_* O_X (equivalently π^{-1}O_Y → O_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the structure used before requiring local conditions; open embeddings and behavior on distinguished bases are described in exercises (e.g., 6.2.A, 6.2.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of schemes should 'look like' maps induced by ring maps on affines
rubrics_metrics.description: Tentative/usable definition: for each affine open Spec A ⊂ X with π(Spec A) ⊂ Spec B ⊂ Y, the induced map of ringed spaces should be of the form coming from a ring map B → A (as in Key Exercise 6.2.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the local affine criterion (6.2.2, 6.3.C) used in practice instead of the more awkward global ringed-space condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of locally ringed spaces (local condition on stalks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally ringed space is a ringed space whose stalks are local rings. A morphism of locally ringed spaces requires that for π(p)=q the induced map on stalks O_{Y,q} → O_{X,p} sends the maximal ideal of O_{Y,q} into the maximal ideal of O_{X,p}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent intuitive condition: functions vanishing at q pull back to functions vanishing at p; consequently nonvanishing at q pulls back to nonvanishing at p as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: morphism of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of schemes is a morphism of locally ringed spaces (equivalently a ringed-space morphism that locally looks like a morphism induced by a ring map on affines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields the category of schemes Sch and the notion of base/structure morphism; in practice one verifies the affine-local condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring maps induce morphisms of (affine) schemes via distinguished open sets
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a ring map π^#: B → A, there is a morphism of ringed spaces (in fact of locally ringed spaces) Spec A → Spec B constructed by describing the map on the distinguished base: on D(g) ⊂ Spec B define O_{Spec B}(D(g)) = B_g → A_{π^# g} = O_{Spec A}(π^{-1}D(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.2.D asks to verify independence of choices and to check that this defines a morphism of sheaves on the distinguished base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of (locally) ringed spaces glue
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is covered by open sets Ui and there are morphisms πi: Ui → Y agreeing on overlaps, then they glue to a unique morphism π: X → Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.2.A and 6.3.A; practical consequence: construct morphisms by describing them on an affine cover and checking compatibility on overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalk-level map for morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a morphism of ringed spaces π: X → Y and p∈X with π(p)=q, there is an induced map of stalks (O_Y)_q → (O_X)_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.2.C indicates the existence and use of these maps; the locally ringed condition places the maximal-ideal-into-maximal-ideal constraint on these stalk maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms Spec A → Spec B of locally ringed spaces determined by global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Proposition 6.3.2: if π: Spec A → Spec B is a morphism of locally ringed spaces then it is the morphism induced by the ring map π^#: B = Γ(Spec B,O) → Γ(Spec A,O) = A (i.e., determined by the map on global sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof idea: the image of a point is determined by which global functions vanish there; the sheaf map is then determined on distinguished opens by localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms X → Spec A correspond to ring maps A → Γ(X,O_X)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural bijection between morphisms X → Spec A and ring morphisms A → Γ(X,O_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential Exercise 6.3.F. In particular the canonical morphism X → Spec Γ(X,O_X) is an isomorphism iff X is affine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and interpretation of Z-valued and A-valued points
rubrics_metrics.description: For a scheme X and scheme Z, the Z-valued points X(Z) are Hom(Z,X); for a ring A, the A-valued points X(A) are Hom(Spec A,X). For affine X=Spec R, X(A) corresponds to solutions in A to polynomial relations defining X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the functor-of-points viewpoint (6.3.7); useful for interpreting rational/integral solutions algebraically: e.g., Q-valued points are rational solutions, Z-valued points integral solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of morphisms to projective space from n+1 functions with no common zeros
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a B-scheme and f0,...,fn are n+1 functions on X with no common zeros, then [f0:...:fn] defines a morphism of B-schemes X → P^n_B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.3.N(a). Moreover if g is nowhere vanishing then [f0:...:fn] and [g f0:...: g fn] define the same morphism (6.3.N(b)). Not every morphism to projective space arises this way unless one allows sections of line bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms from Spec of a local ring
rubrics_metrics.description: For a local ring (A,m), morphisms Spec A → X correspond bijectively to pairs (p ∈ X, local homomorphisms O_{X,p} → A) with image of the closed point [m] equal to p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.3.M gives the precise bijection and suggests that any open set containing p contains the image of such a morphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maps of graded rings induce maps of Proj under V(φ(S+)) = ∅
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ: S• → R• is a map of graded rings (preserving grading up to a fixed factor) then φ induces a morphism Proj R• \ V(φ(S+)) → Proj S•; in particular if V(φ(S+)) = ∅ then φ induces a morphism Proj R• → Proj S•.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 6.4.A constructs the maps on distinguished opens D(φ(x)) → D(x) for homogeneous x and checks they glue; hypotheses about images of positive-degree parts are important (see 6.4.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Veronese subring and Proj invariance under regrading
rubrics_metrics.description: For S• a finitely generated graded ring, the nth Veronese subring S^{(n)} = ⊕_j S_{nj} yields Proj S^{(n)} ≅ Proj S• (when degrees align appropriately); one can regrade to ensure generation in degree 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 6.4.D–6.4.G explain constructing the Veronese, showing isomorphism of Proj, and finding a d so that regraded ring is generated in new degree 1; practical consequence: many Proj constructions are insensitive to finitely many degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not every morphism to projective space comes from global functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even the identity morphism P^1_k → P^1_k cannot be given by n+1 global functions with no common zeros when the source has no nonconstant global functions; one must use sections of line bundles (Theorem 16.4.1 gives the correct generalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion around 6.3.10: global functions are insufficient in general; consider line-bundle-valued sections for a universal description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rational maps: morphisms defined almost everywhere for reduced schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A rational map is informally a morphism defined on a dense open subset (i.e., defined almost everywhere). For this section X is assumed reduced; good situations make rational maps uniquely determined where defined and give a largest domain of definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the start of §6.5 and later references (Reduced-to-Separated Theorem 10.2.2 and 6.5.6).
